rationale: The en-US "Search image with Google Lens" is a button label; other button labels in this file use the infinitive (e.g. "Pořídit fotografii"), not the 2nd-person imperative.
summary: Accessibility label is rendered as an imperative addressed to the user instead of a noun-style label describing the button.

rationale: AddressToolbar.SearchEngine.A11y.Hint.v133 in the same file renders "search engine" as "vyhledávač"; the same term on the same control should be consistent.
summary: "Search Engine" is translated as "Vyhledávací modul" while the neighbouring string uses "vyhledávač".

rationale: Other strings in the same file (Bookmarks.Menu.SavedBookmarkToastLabel.v136) correctly use Czech quotes „…“; here the English closing-style quotes are kept, which is inconsistent typography for cs.
summary: Uses English-style straight/curly quotes instead of Czech quotation marks used elsewhere in the same file.

rationale: Czech typography uses an en/em dash (–) for parenthetical breaks, matching the source's em dash; a plain hyphen is incorrect.
summary: Em dash from the source replaced with a hyphen surrounded by spaces.

rationale: The source says "passwords"; the rest of the feature strings use "hesla", and "přihlašovací údaje" corresponds to logins/credentials.
summary: "passwords" translated as "přihlašovacích údajů" (login credentials).

rationale: The field asks for the name of a neighbourhood/district within a city; Czech uses "Čtvrť" (or "Městská část"). "Sousedství" means proximity/neighbourliness and is not an address component.
summary: "Neighborhood" as an address field is mistranslated as "Sousedství" (the abstract concept of neighbourliness/proximity), not a city district.

rationale: The comment says the field holds the organization's name, which may be any organization, not only a commercial company; Czech has the direct equivalent "Organizace".
summary: "Organization" is rendered as "Společnost" (company), narrowing the meaning.

rationale: The en-US is an imperative call to action; "Začnete" is the 2nd person plural future indicative ("you will start"), a typo for the imperative "Začněte".
summary: Imperative "Start your first search" rendered as future indicative "Začnete" instead of imperative "Začněte".

rationale: The certificate field is the issuer Organization (O); the Czech term is "Organizace", not "Společnost" (company).
summary: "Organization" translated as "Společnost" (company) instead of "Organizace".

rationale: The certificate field is a DNS name of the subject, not a DNS record; "Záznam" means record.
summary: "DNS Name" translated as "Záznam DNS" (DNS record).

rationale: The active participle "sledující" means "watching"; the established Czech Firefox term for tracking content is "sledovací obsah", consistent with "sledovací prvky" used elsewhere in this file.
summary: "Tracking content" is translated as "Sledující obsah" (content that tracks/watches) instead of the standard Firefox term "Sledovací obsah".

rationale: Source is "Leave no traces on this device"; the Czech omits "on this device" and renders it as "(It) leaves no traces".
suggest: Nezanechávejte na tomto zařízení žádné stopy
summary: The translation drops "on this device" and changes the imperative to a third-person statement.

rationale: Source "%1$@ tabs closed: %2$@" means tabs were closed in the named app (%1$@ = app name, %2$@ = number of tabs); the Czech reads "Firefox closed tabs: <number>" attributing the action to the app and losing the count relation.
summary: The notification title is mistranslated: %1$@ is the app name, and the Czech turns it into the app closing tabs rather than "tabs closed in <app>: <count>".

rationale: The developer comment says this is a label for an action; en-US "View recently closed tabs" is a verb phrase, and Czech action labels use the infinitive/imperative.
summary: Action label rendered as a noun ("Zobrazení") instead of an imperative verb for a button action.

rationale: Czech typography requires „…“ quotation marks; the English style “…” was copied from the source.
summary: Straight/English quotation marks used instead of Czech quotes.

current: od anonymního prohlížení po ukládání akcí
rationale: The source lists features from private browsing to save actions (i.e. actions that save content); the Czech genitive reverses the relation and says "saving actions".
suggest: od anonymního prohlížení po akce ukládání
summary: "save actions" (actions for saving) is mistranslated as "ukládání akcí" (saving of actions).

rationale: The accessibility label must state the target (Customize Homepage); "Přizpůsobit" alone means merely "Customize" and loses the content.
summary: "Customize Homepage" is rendered only as "Přizpůsobit", dropping the object of the accessibility label.

rationale: The developer comment states this is the Zoom tool that applies zoom on a page, not a window; other strings in the same submenu use "Zvětšení stránky".
summary: "Zoom" (page zoom) is translated as "Zvětšit okno" (enlarge window), which names the wrong object and conflicts with the related Zoom strings.

rationale: The comment says this subtitle is for the Zoom tool (zoom on a page); "okno" (window) is the wrong object and the same screen uses "Zvětšení stránky".
summary: "Zoom" is rendered as "Zvětšit okno" (enlarge window) instead of page zoom, inconsistent with the sibling Zoom title strings.

rationale: In the source "For good." pairs with "Indie. Non-profit." and means acting for the common good, not "forever".
summary: "For good." is rendered as "Navždy." (forever), losing the intended "for the good of all / for good causes" meaning.

rationale: The developer comment states %2$@ is the company name (e.g. Mozilla); labelling it as an application is wrong content.
summary: %2$@ is the company name (Mozilla), but the Czech calls it "aplikace" (the app).

rationale: Czech button labels must be grammatically consistent; "Souhlasím a pokračovat" mixes 1st-person indicative with an infinitive, which is ungrammatical.
summary: Mismatched constructions: finite verb "Souhlasím" coordinated with infinitive "pokračovat".

rationale: The option describes where the toolbar is placed; the parallel option is "Dole" (at the bottom) and the v145 variant of the same string correctly uses "Nahoře". "Nahoru" means "upwards" (direction).
summary: "Top" (position of the toolbar) is rendered as directional "Nahoru" (upwards) instead of locative "Nahoře" (at the top).

current: Vydejte se s aplikací %@ za dobrodružstvím
rationale: The source emphasizes taking the app along on all browsing adventures; the translation omits both "all" and "browsing".
suggest: Vydejte se s aplikací %@ za všemi svými dobrodružstvími při prohlížení
summary: "on all your browsing adventures" is reduced to "za dobrodružstvím", dropping "all your browsing".

current: Přináší nezisková organizace %@, které důvěřujete již více než 20 let
rationale: The source says the non-profit has been trusted (generally, by people) for over 20 years, not that the reader personally has trusted it for 20 years.
suggest: Přináší nezisková organizace %@, které se důvěřuje již více než 20 let
summary: "trusted for over 20 years" is rendered as "které důvěřujete" (which you have trusted), changing the meaning and attributing trust to the individual user.

rationale: The v145 source changed from "Manage" to "Manage settings"; the Czech only says "Settings", losing the manage action.
summary: "Manage settings" is translated as just "Nastavení" (Settings), dropping the verb.

current: Vyberte si tapetu, která vás vyjadřuje.
rationale: The English means a wallpaper that appeals to/resonates with the user; "která vás vyjadřuje" says the wallpaper expresses the user, which is a different statement and ungrammatical in sense.
suggest: Vyberte si tapetu, která vás osloví.
summary: "a wallpaper that speaks to you" mistranslated as "tapetu, která vás vyjadřuje" (a wallpaper that expresses you).

current: Další informace naleznete v našich oznámeních o ochraně osobních údajů
rationale: The source refers to one document, the Privacy Notice; the same file translates "Privacy Notice" as "Zásady ochrany osobních údajů" (Onboarding.TermsOfService.PrivacyNoticeLink.v135). The plural "oznámeních" is both wrong in number and terminologically inconsistent.
suggest: Další informace naleznete v našich zásadách ochrany osobních údajů
summary: "privacy notice" (singular document) rendered as plural "oznámeních o ochraně osobních údajů", inconsistent with the term used elsewhere in the same file.

rationale: Source is "Cross-Site Tracking Cookies"; the Czech omits the cross-site qualifier, which is the key distinguishing part of this Privacy Dashboard category.
summary: "Cross-Site" is dropped, so the label no longer distinguishes cross-site tracking cookies.

rationale: Body.Text.v112 translates "survey" as "dotazník"; the button on the same popup must use the same term.
summary: Button uses "průzkum" while the body text of the same popup calls it "dotazník", an inconsistent term for "survey" on one screen.

rationale: en-US "Save Cards to %@" is plural; the Czech says "save a payment card" (singular). Compare the parallel address string "Uložit adresy do %@".
summary: Plural "Cards" rendered as singular "platební kartu" and "do aplikace" added.

current: %@ náhodně vybírá uživatele, aby otestoval nové funkce, s cílem zlepšit jeho kvalitu pro všechny.
rationale: Source: "randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone." The Czech singular "aby otestoval" makes the app the tester instead of the users, and "zlepšit jeho kvalitu" adds a possessive not in the source.
suggest: %@ náhodně vybírá uživatele, aby otestovali nové funkce, což zlepšuje kvalitu pro všechny.
summary: The translation says quality is improved "for it" (the app) rather than "for everyone", and the subject of testing is wrong.

rationale: "Informace o kartě" is plural here; the predicate must agree: "byly aktualizovány".
summary: Subject–verb agreement error: "Informace" (plural) with singular verb form.

rationale: The other "Sent from %2$@" strings use the impersonal "Odesláno"; "Odeslané" is an adjectival plural form that does not agree with anything here.
summary: Inconsistent/incorrect participle form "Odeslané" instead of "Odesláno" as used in the parallel strings.

current: Klepnutím a podržením zobrazíte zobrazení čtečky.
rationale: The en-US "Touch and hold for Reader View" is rendered with a redundant repetition ("zobrazíte zobrazení"), degrading the language.

summary: Awkward duplication "zobrazíte zobrazení čtečky" and it repeats "Klepnutím" for "Touch and hold".

current: Tato stránka je buď s omezením nebo se jedná převážně o vizuální stránku.
rationale: Czech punctuation requires a comma before "nebo" in the "buď…, nebo…" pair; the phrase "je buď s omezením" is also ungrammatical.
suggest: Tato stránka může být omezená, nebo se jedná převážně o vizuální obsah.
summary: Missing comma before "nebo" in the correlative "buď … nebo" construction and clumsy wording.

rationale: The source button label is "Sync Tabs"; the Czech omits "panely", losing the specific meaning of syncing tabs.

rationale: The same source term "Privacy Notice" appears in TermsOfUse.Description.v142 as "Oznámení o ochraně osobních údajů"; the link label must match on the same screen.
summary: "Privacy Notice" is translated as "Zásady ochrany osobních údajů" here but as "Oznámení o ochraně osobních údajů" in the description on the same sheet.

current: Přehled s Podmínkami používání byl otevřen

summary: Uses "Podmínkami používání" while every other string in the same file uses "Podmínky použití".

rationale: Source is a verb phrase describing the button action; Czech renders it as a noun, and it also collides with "Souhrn stránky" usage elsewhere.

rationale: En-US "Card Information Updated" is rendered with the plural noun "informace" but a singular participle/verb; Czech requires "byly aktualizovány".

summary: "Whether or not your device is a tablet" mistranslated as "Bez ohledu na to, zda..." ("Regardless of whether...").

rationale: Source uses an em dash separator; Czech typography requires an en/em dash, not a hyphen, between clauses.

rationale: en-US is "Search with Firefox"; the Czech only says "Search", losing the product name.
